own_scenes.desc: A mediados de los ochenta el público del este y del oeste volvió a juntarse en clubes del centro como el Liedernacht del viejo Leland Hotel, con negros, blancos, heteros y gays. Su padre fue Ken Collier, DJ forjado en la era disco, figura paterna de los chavales de las fiestas y de la comunidad gay de Detroit. Con su hermano Greg pinchó los primeros discos de techno («Strings of Life», «No UFOs») en Todd’s; luego reinó en Heaven y, cuando ardió, en Times Square. Sin trucos, solo con el instinto de lo que funcionaba y un vaso de coñac, convertía una noche en una experiencia religiosa. Murió en 1996 por una diabetes diagnosticada tarde, cuando empezaba a tocar en citas como el Mayday de Berlín.

refs.q: Ken was the first person to champion Detroit techno. He and his brother Greg spun the first techno records [“Strings of Life,” “No UFOs,” etc.] at the club Todd’s, a dance music mecca that exposed the masses to new music [punk, new wave, industrial, and house on alternate nights]. After Todd’s closed, Ken held sway at Heaven, a second-floor club that’s not a mile from where I live. His “children” lived to hear him play week after week.

refs.q: When it was black and gay, before it became fashionable and suburban.
refs.para: He also was a resident at Times Square, a downtown club where his “children” followed him after Heaven burned down. He was a great champion of our music, in the great black music tradition. When it was black and gay, before it became fashionable and suburban.
